title: Seller Bridge Accelerant Playbook (draft)
body:
Intent: ultra-concise slide pack + battlecard for SEs and SDRs to accelerate pilot decisions when buyers are stuck between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Not final — sketch for testing in SE office hours.

Deck structure (slide-by-slide rough notes)
- Slide 1: Title + positioning
  - "Seller Bridge": accelerate buyer to a safe pilot decision in 1 meeting.
  - One-line value prop: reduce inference risk by mapping buyer constraints to the smallest viable deployment.
  - Speaker note: lead with customer's top constraint (latency / compliance / cost).

- Slide 2: Decision ladder (visual)
  - Row 1: Constraint check (Latency | Data residency | Throughput | Budget | SLA)
  - Row 2: Recommended immediate pilot mode (Hosted API -> Dedicated -> Private) with expected tradeoff callouts.
  - Quick numbers: hosted = fastest (48–72h), dedicated = predictable (2–4 weeks), private = regulated (4–8 weeks).
  - Speaker note: use this to structure qualifying questions.

- Slide 3: 90-minute pilot playbook (operational cadence)
  - Phase A (Kickoff, 0–2 days): scope success metric, sample traffic, minimal dataset access method.
  - Phase B (Run, 1–14 days): test traffic patterns, real prompt set, measure latency P95, token cost delta.
  - Phase C (Review, 14–21 days): present outcomes and next-step recommendation.
  - Callouts: fallback plan (hosted variant + lower-cost quantized model) if throughput or cost fails.

- Slide 4: Rapid technical checklist (what SEs run in first call)
  - Checkpoint: Is PII/sensitive data in prompts? If yes, escalate to security and consider Private or Dedicated with encryption.
  - Latency test: ask for worst-case end-to-end roundtrip and sample size.
  - Throughput: peak concurrent requests and average length in tokens.
  - Budget envelope: absolute monthly spend cap.
  - Speaker note: write down answers verbatim — these become the pilot acceptance criteria.

- Slide 5: Fallback decision matrix (one-card battlecard)
  - If latency requirement <=150ms P95 -> prefer Dedicated in-region or Hosted with regional routing + model variant.
  - If strict data residency/compliance -> Private or Dedicated with VPC, list docs to reference.
  - If budget < $X/month for expected QPS -> try caching/prefix reuse and smaller quantized models first.
  - SE quick script: "If we hit X latency or Y cost, here are our three automated fallback steps we can push live for you."

- Slide 6: Objection rebut scripts (short)
  - "We don’t want vendor-managed data" -> "We offer Private with customer-managed KMS and audit logs; here’s the SOC2 link."
  - "Dedicated is too slow to provision" -> "We can stage a hosted pilot while dedicated is configured; runtime-level fallbacks keep production calls safe."
  - "Quantized models are lower quality" -> "We run A/B on a small signal set and report quality deltas; typical instruction-tuned models retain >95% task accuracy for short prompts."

- Slide 7: Evidence snippets (one-liners for slide or call)
  - Customer example: midmarket SaaS used hosted -> dedicated over 6 weeks, 2x throughput with 30% cost improvement after batching/caching. (anonymized)
  - Metric cards: typical P95 improvements with Dedicated in-region: 20–40ms; caching reduces token cost by 18–40% depending on prompt reuse.

- Slide 8: Playbook appendix (ops hooks)
  - Canary script template (copy/paste into Ops runbook).
  - Required info to open a pilot ticket: model-id, expected qps, sample prompts, acceptable latency, billing owner.
  - Contact matrix: SE -> Solutions Eng -> Platform Eng -> Customer Success with Slack handles.

Battlecard (single page extract for quick clipboard)
- Topline: "What to say when buyer asks: ‘How do we reduce risk and time to results?’"
  - Answer: "Run a 2-week hosted pilot to validate quality while we stand up a Dedicated lane in parallel; if data residency or compliance blocks hosted, we fast-track Private scoping and use an on-prem smoke test."
- Rapid qualifying script (30s)
  - "Three quick questions: 1) Any sensitive data? 2) What’s your avg/max tokens? 3) Rough monthly spend cap?"
- Quick fallback sequence (operationally safe)
  - 1) Route to cheaper model variant + enable KV caching.
  - 2) Throttle/batch non-interactive traffic, preserve low-latency tail for primary UI.
  - 3) Failover to regionally compatible hosted model if Dedicated capacity delayed.

Open questions / gaps to fill before SE silver-bullet release
- Get up-to-date quantized model quality numbers from Applied ML (Nikhil P).
- Prepare SOC/KMS one-pager for compliance objections (Security).
- Scripted Slack alerts and runbook entries for pilot canary (SRE/Platform).

Next steps (for this draft)
- Validate wording in SE office hours 2025-02-06.
- Ask Solutions Eng to bake the canary template into the pilot repo.
- Run 2 live mock calls with conversation recordings to refine rebut scripts (assign: Tom).

Notes to self (rough brainstorm fragments)
- Could add a tiny decision-tree flowchart + color coding for friction severity.
- Consider a 1-click checklist in Console that populates the pilot ticket fields from this pack.
- Keep wording short — SEs want 60–90s soundbites.

References / links
- Confluence: INF-PLATFORM-1963 (pilot standards)
- Jira: GTMSUP-470 (pilot playbook epic)
- GitHub: repo/redwood/pilot-scripts#12 (canary template)

Raw slack snippets to include (copyable)
- "If we see latency >150ms P95 during the pilot we will: 1) enable regional routing; 2) swap to quantized variant; 3) enable cache TTL=30s for repeated prompts — we'll notify you within 15 mins."

End.
